description.p: Natter Den shows WhatsApp Web in a GTK 4 and libadwaita window, with desktop notifications, a tray icon and keyboard shortcuts.
Natter Den is unofficial. It isn’t made by, endorsed by or affiliated with WhatsApp or Meta. You link it to your phone as a linked device, as you would WhatsApp Web in a browser.

ul.li: One notification per chat, with the sender’s picture; clicking it opens that chat
Quiet hours, and Do not disturb for one hour, two or until you turn it off
The unread count in the tray, and on the dock icon where the dock shows badges (not in the Flatpak)
Ctrl+K goes to a chat by name, or messages a phone number without saving it
Paste or drop pictures and files on a chat
whatsapp:// links from other apps open in Natter Den
A privacy blur that hides names, pictures and messages until you point at them
An app lock with a passcode
Several accounts, each with its own session
Closing the window keeps it running in the tray

description.p: Replying from a notification and calls are experimental. Calls use WhatsApp’s own call buttons: in Natter Den’s window when GStreamer’s WebRTC plugins are installed, otherwise in a separate call window if Qt WebEngine for Python is installed, or else in your web browser.
A lighter privacy blur, steadier calls, and a dependency check for every distribution.

ul.li: Privacy blur without a graphics filter, and a cover (not a blur) while another window is in front: both cost next to nothing now
Other apps' audio pauses while you record a voice message, and plays again after
Calls: packets leave from their own thread, a network-process loss waits for the call to end, incoming calls are recognised in more languages, and the log says why every reload happened
The installer checks and names every piece calls, videos, sound and the camera need, on Arch, Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora and openSUSE
The problem report lists graphics-driver hangs from the previous boot too
Replies from a notification are confirmed by more of WhatsApp's current page: the chat list's open chat, the notified message without WhatsApp's old markup, and the chat's picture
The page lent to the reply card is drawn, so WhatsApp keeps working while a reply is sent

description.p: Fixes for replying from notifications and for call sound.

ul.li: Replying from a notification works with WhatsApp's current page, also with the window closed (still experimental)
Fewer clicks in call sound after a silence, with WebKitGTK before 2.54.2 and GStreamer 1.28
A call keeps going through short reconnections, with less background work while it runs

description.p: First release. So far it has been run on Ada 26.04 and on CachyOS with KDE Plasma.

ul.li: One notification per chat, quiet hours and Do not disturb
Ctrl+K to go to a chat or message a phone number
A privacy blur and an app lock
Several accounts, each with its own session
Experimental: replying from a notification, calls, and a Flatpak
